name: IC 3583 (Hubble)
blurb: IC 3583, an irregular dwarf galaxy, seen by Hubble.
label: ic3583-hubble
story: IC 3583 looks like a loose scatter of stars, yet a bar of stars runs through its center. On the sky it pairs with the great spiral Messier 90, though Hubble distances place it well in front of that galaxy.

claims.text: It has a bar of stars through its center
With Messier 90 it forms the pair Arp 76
Arp 76 is an optical pair; NGC 4569 lies behind IC 3583
HST distances put IC 3583 in front of the Virgo cluster
